name: Multifocal Peripheral Venous Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Venous Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of multiple venous malformations located in peripheral soft tissues
Characteristic imaging findings on MRI or ultrasound showing slow-flow venous channels with phleboliths
Soft, compressible, bluish lesions that enlarge with dependency or Valsalva maneuver
Lack of arterial flow on Doppler ultrasound differentiating from arteriovenous malformations
Histological confirmation showing dilated, thin-walled venous channels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multifocal peripheral venous lesions with characteristic imaging findings and clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be considered in syndromic cases but is not routinely required.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple soft compressible bluish venous lesions
Lesion enlargement with dependency or Valsalva maneuver
searchTerms: lesion grows when standing or straining
swelling increases with position or pressure
mass enlarges with dependency or Valsalva

common.symptomName: Localized pain or tenderness at lesion sites

occasional.symptomName: Functional impairment due to lesion size or location
Nerve compression symptoms adjacent to lesions

rare.symptomName: Bleeding or ulceration of overlying skin
Deep venous thrombosis secondary to venous stasis
searchTerms: deep vein clots from slow blood flow

rare.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure in extensive cases
searchTerms: heart failure from high blood flow

laboratory: Normal coagulation profile unless thrombophlebitis present
D-dimer may be elevated in thrombosis
imaging: MRI showing slow-flow venous malformations with characteristic T2 hyperintensity
Ultrasound Doppler demonstrating absence of arterial flow and presence of phleboliths
Plain radiographs may reveal phlebolith calcifications
genetic: Somatic mutations in TEK (TIE2) gene reported in some cases
other: Histopathology showing dilated, thin-walled venous channels without arterial components

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of high-flow arterial components on Doppler ultrasound

redFlags: Rapid lesion enlargement with pain and warmth suggesting thrombosis or infection
Signs of deep venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism
references: Wassef M, Blei F, Adams DM, et al. Vascular anomalies classification: recommendations from the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e203-e214.
